cta.cta_text: Talk through your questions with an Edstellar assessment specialist.

items.question: What is an employee engagement survey?
items.answer: An employee engagement survey, a focused kind of employee survey, measures how committed, energized and supported people feel at work, going beyond employee satisfaction, and which drivers, such as growth, recognition and manager support, shape that experience. Edstellar designs surveys that lead to clear action by leaders and managers.

items.question: What is the difference between an annual engagement survey and a pulse survey?
items.answer: An annual survey gives a full, organization-wide view of engagement and its drivers. Pulse surveys are short and frequent, keeping a steady read on key drivers between annual surveys. Edstellar often combines both.

items.question: Which tools does Edstellar use for engagement surveys?
items.answer: Edstellar designs tailored engagement surveys and uses Mindgage for ongoing pulse feedback. Where engagement is assessed alongside culture and inclusion, Talogy Perceptions can be added.

items.question: How do you protect anonymity?
items.answer: Anonymity safeguards, such as minimum group sizes for reporting, are agreed at scoping and explained to employees before the survey. Survey results are used to improve the workplace, never to single out individuals, so people can answer an anonymous employee survey openly.

items.question: How do you make sure results lead to action?
items.answer: Every manager receives clear results for their team and support to discuss them, and teams agree on two or three practical actions. Pulse checks then track progress, so employees see what changed because of their feedback.

items.question: How often should we run an engagement survey?
items.answer: Many organizations run a full survey once a year, with short pulse checks in between. Edstellar recommends a rhythm that gives a steady read without asking people too often and keeps each engagement initiative on track.

items.question: Can you run onboarding and exit surveys?
items.answer: Yes. Onboarding and exit surveys capture feedback at key moments, showing what helps new joiners settle in and what influences people to stay or leave.

items.question: How is an engagement survey different from a culture assessment?
items.answer: An engagement survey measures how committed and energized employees feel. A culture assessment looks at the values, behaviors and leadership climate behind that experience. Edstellar offers both, and they work well together.

items.question: How long does an engagement survey take?
items.answer: Most organizations have their results within about six weeks of kickoff. Manager action planning and pulse checks then continue over the following months.

items.question: How is engagement survey data protected?
items.answer: Survey data is collected only for the agreed purpose, access is limited to agreed stakeholders, and results are reported under the anonymity and confidentiality terms set at scoping. Edstellar holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification for information security management.

items.question: How much does an employee engagement survey cost?
items.answer: Cost depends on the number of employees and locations, the survey formats, how often you run pulse checks, and how much reporting and action-planning support you need. Edstellar scopes each survey program before quoting, so you pay only for what your goals require.
